scope: MC-014/015/018/019/021/022/025 selected public service, approval, scoped memory and transaction completion contracts; final mandatory combined command subset plus exact before-repair counterexamples.
sourceState: Final owned production source frozen; final mandatory local dirty-candidate run. This is not clean-HEAD MCD acceptance, native CNB pipeline evidence or formal RDAS276 acceptance.
dataMode: synthetic sandbox; loopback real PostgreSQL with disposable 43-migration databases and genuine app/gateway roles; six declared pure unit cases
deduplication: 75 distinct final mandatory test cases. Earlier 55/55 and 20/20 runs support development history; 22/22 related and service reruns are subsets and are not added again.

reproduction.requiredEnvironment: BMS_PG_TEST_URL must point to an explicitly disposable loopback test administrator database. Service cases require the full migration set and app/gateway roles; use the repository .db-gate sequence for the complete setup. No production URL is accepted by the owned synthetic fixture.

additionalFixtureFailureCheck.preconditions: Fresh unmigrated disposable loopback PostgreSQL database, absent tenants table, actual fixture import/pools and captured original environment.

Controlled acknowledgement faults model transport uncertainty around real PostgreSQL statements; they do not measure failure frequency in production.
A COMMIT acknowledgement loss rejects the call even if the server committed; retries read durable state and dedupe. The report does not promise every rejected COMMIT means no data persisted.
Legacy global memory keys remain unchanged; scoped new keys do not migrate or remove old rows.

Other inherited transaction helpers, including db.withWorkspace/readPrefs/recall, were not systematically fault-tested by this bounded repair scope. A matching code pattern is a D-level risk until independently reproduced.
